title: Heart anatomy: chambers, valves and blood flow
description: A four-chambered muscular pump with four valves and its own electrical conduction system.

questions.question: How many chambers does the heart have?
questions.answer: The heart has two upper receiving chambers, the right and left atria, and two lower pumping chambers, the right and left ventricles. The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs; the left sends it to the body.

questions.question: What route does blood take through the heart?
questions.answer: Blood returns from the body to the right atrium, passes the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle, then crosses the pulmonary valve to the lungs. Oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium, passes the mitral valve to the left ventricle and leaves through the aortic valve.

questions.question: Why is the left ventricular wall thicker?
questions.answer: The left ventricle must generate greater pressure to move blood through the systemic circulation. Its myocardium is therefore thicker than that of the right ventricle, which pumps into the lower-pressure pulmonary circulation.

questions.question: Do coronary arteries carry blood through the heart chambers?
questions.answer: No. Coronary arteries branch near the aortic root and supply the heart muscle itself. The blood passing through the chambers does not directly nourish the full thickness of the myocardium.

questions.question: How do heart valves keep blood moving forward?
questions.answer: Tricuspid and mitral valves guard the atrioventricular openings; pulmonary and aortic valves guard ventricular outflow. They open and close in response to pressure changes, limiting backward flow rather than actively pumping blood.
